bands.note: 1 GHz. Far down the Rayleigh–Jeans tail of everything here, where brightness is simply proportional to temperature — so nothing is cut off, and the image is the scene’s temperature map at low gain.
bands.label: Radio

bands.note: 100 GHz. Still Rayleigh–Jeans for every source in this scene, so it differs from radio only in sensitivity. That similarity is the real physics, not a shortcut.
bands.label: Microwave

bands.note: 10 µm. The coolest band with a Wien cutoff that bites in this scene: material below ~1500 K begins to fade while stars and the disc stay bright.
bands.label: Infrared

bands.note: 550 nm. True colour — the frame exactly as rendered, with no remapping.
bands.label: Visible

bands.note: 200 nm. The cutoff bites hard: cool K and M stars all but vanish while hot A/B stars and the inner accretion disc blaze.
bands.label: Ultraviolet

bands.note: 0.3 keV soft X-ray. Only million-kelvin material survives — the inner disc and neutron-star surfaces. Ordinary stars are black silhouettes.
bands.label: X-ray

bands.note: ~100 keV. Nothing thermal in this scene is hot enough to reach here, so the frame goes black. Real gamma sources are non-thermal (synchrotron, pair processes), which this model does not simulate.
bands.label: Gamma

crafts.name: Saturn V / Apollo
crafts.blurb: Three stages, 2 970 t on the pad, 111 m tall. The S-IVB restarts for translunar injection; the CSM and LM ride under the fairing.

crafts.name: Falcon 9 Block 5
crafts.blurb: Nine Merlins, a recoverable first stage with grid fins and legs, and a hoverslam that has to be solved for rather than scripted — minimum throttle gives TWR > 1, so it cannot hover.

crafts.name: Space Shuttle
crafts.blurb: Two solids that cannot be shut down, three engines fed from a tank that is not part of the orbiter, and a wing that only matters for the last twenty minutes of the mission.

crafts.name: Starship / Super Heavy
crafts.blurb: 33 Raptors under 3 400 t of methalox. Both stages return: the booster to the tower, the ship belly-first through the atmosphere and then flipped upright in the last seconds.

crafts.name: Apollo Lunar Module
crafts.blurb: Two stages: a throttleable descent stage that lands, and an ascent stage that uses it as a launch pad. Descent follows the real P63 / P64 / P66 program sequence and its published gate conditions.

crafts.name: Mars EDL — Sky Crane
crafts.blurb: Entry at 5.8 km/s behind a heat shield, a supersonic chute at Mach 1.7, then a descent stage that lowers the rover on cables and flies away to crash somewhere else.

crafts.name: Ion Cruiser (Dawn-class)
crafts.blurb: Three NEXT gridded ion engines and 425 kg of xenon. A quarter of a newton of thrust — a tenth the weight of a postcard — held for months at a time, which is why it can visit two main-belt worlds on one tank.

crafts.name: Hail Mary
crafts.blurb: Three parallel astrophage tanks around a central spine, a pressure vessel forward of them, and a nose that holds four beetles. Four spin drives on one thrust plane, 1.5 g and 2 000 t of fuel — enough to reach Tau Ceti in thirteen Earth years and six and a half aboard.

crafts.name: Beetle probe
crafts.blurb: A one-way courier: no crew, no life support, and a mass ratio the Hail Mary itself cannot reach. It is the only part of the mission that was always going to make it home.

text.blurb: Three suns, one world. A tight binary (Alpha + Beta) with Trisolaris on a wide eccentric circumbinary orbit, and hot Gamma sweeping past every 51 years. Insolation swings 9× — the Stable and Chaotic Eras are emergent, not scripted. Stable for 60 000+ years.
